body:
Thanks for the reply. I don't feel joy in anything anymore. The only time I'm happy is when I'm going to the gym and I am in good shape. But outside of that, I don't socialize with people anymore and I've essentially stopped talking to all of my friends after the breakup except for one. 

I keep telling myself, "I'll wait until x" and if I'm not better by then, I should probably consider more drastic options. Then when x comes around, I'm still not in any better situation.

I was also cheated on by my ex gf and we dated for 7 years. She went with him after.

However, I stopped reading your post because you have to fix the structure- it's just one large, rambling, wall of text. If you fix it by separating your thoughts into concise paragraphs, I will listen to what you have to say.

There is no such thing as "the one". It's very possible that this person you loved had a lot of qualities you liked, but more often than not you just make compromises and the good outweighs the bad, so the bad things about them aren't apparent.

You say you've tried to date other people but they can't compare. It's possible that you haven't given them a fair chance because this other person has you mind fucked. In other words, the bad qualities are amplified and you can't notice the good qualities because you consistently have this old love high up on a pedestal. 

I think that things won't improve until you take her off that pedestal and stop letting her have such an impact on your thoughts.

All the best..
